annotations.title: Confeſsing their ſinnes.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> A certaine confeſſion of ſinnes there was euen in that penance which Iohn preached, and which was made before men were baptized. Whereby it is cleere that Iohn made a preparation to the Sacrament of Penance which afterward was inſtituted by Chriſt, as wel as he did by baptizing prepare the way to Chriſts baptiſme.

annotations.title: Their ſinnes.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> He doth not ſay that they confeſſed them ſelues to be ſinners, which may be done by a general confeſſion: but that they confeſſed their ſinnes, which is a particular confeſſion.

annotations.title: Clothed.
annotations.text: ◦ The Holy Ghoſt thought it worthy of ſpeciall reporting how ſtraitly this Prophete liued, and how he abſtained from delicate meates and apparel. See Mat. c. 3,

annotations.title: With water.
annotations.text: [1] Iohn with water only, Chriſt with the Holy Ghoſt, not only, as the Heretikes hold, that ſay water is not neceſſary, [2]but with water and the Holy Ghoſt, as it is plaine Io. 3. vnles a man be borne againe of water and the Holy Ghoſt, he ſhal not enter into the kingdom of heauen.

annotations.title: Baptized of Iohn.
annotations.text: The humility of Chriſt not diſdaining his ſeruants baptiſme. Which is an example for al faithful not to diſdaine Chriſts Sacraments of any Prieſt be he neuer ſo ſimple, being by the Catholike Church lawfully called. Aug. li. 5 de bapt. c. 9.

annotations.title: The Spirit.
annotations.text: ◦ Expreſſe mention of the B. Trinitie. the Father ſpeaketh from heauen, the Holy Ghoſt appeareth in the likeneſſe of a doue, the Sonne alſo is recommended vnto vs. Ambros. li. 1 de Sacram. c. 5.

annotations.title: Deſert.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Chriſt doing penance by long faſting, ſolitarineſſe, and conuerſing with wilde beaſtes, gaue example and inſtruction to the Church for Lent faſt, and to holy Eremites of retiring them ſelues to the wilderneſſe and prayer.

annotations.title: Deſert place.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Chriſt vſed very often to retire into ſolitary places, no doubt for our example, to teach vs that ſuch places are beſt for prayer and contemplation, and that we ſhould often retire our ſelues from worldly matters to ſolitary meditation of heauenly things.
